maya: heads-up: P90 for text-gen-prod/us-west jumped ~8x in the last 12m, from ~120ms -> ~950ms. Users reporting slow responses. Investigating now.
chris: saw that too. graphs show big queue depth on the provisioner. autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough. possible warm pool depletion?
jin: adding that we pushed kernel-selection tweak ~40m ago to reduce jitter on longer sequences. could be an interaction with new batching heuristic.
infra-bot: deploy: r-inference/runtime@release-2026-03-18 deployed by chris at 2026-03-18T09:42:11Z :rocket:
maya: ok note that timing. 40m is consistent.
chris: also seeing high KV cache miss rate correlating with the latency spike (per-host counters). looks like instances coming up without warmed KV cache.
jin: noisy neighbor hypothesis: some nodes in the warm pool are scheduled on a multi-tenant rack experiencing PCIe reschedule spikes. perf counters show periodic NVLINK resets on a subset.
sre-oncall: @maya can you share a span/trace id for a slow request so we can look up runtime traces?
maya: trace: trace-id=trc_0b8f2a6c; sample slow request attached below.
maya: ```
2026-03-18T09:41:23.512Z pid=7128 req=trc_0b8f2a6c stage=kernel-select time_ms=170 queue_ms=240 kv_lookup_ms=430 gpu_infer_ms=90
2026-03-18T09:41:23.704Z pid=7128 req=trc_0b8f2a6c error=autoprovision_timeout
```
chris: that kv_lookup_ms=430 is huge. indicates cache miss workflows + provisioning blocking.
jin: quick question — are we still using the conservative batching window (15ms) in us-west? If batching window increased recently, could make tail latencies worse when warm pool is low.
maya: config for us-west at the time: `batch_window_ms=10, max_batch_tokens=4096, warm_pool_target=18`
chris: warm_pool_target=18 seems insufficient for current qps burst pattern after policy change. autoscaler backoff also has a 30s stabilization delay.
sre-oncall: I see scale events: new instance launches at 09:40:55, first health-check pass 09:41:50, assigned traffic 09:41:55. ~60s provisioning lag.
devex: workaround idea: increase warm_pool_target to 30 and disable conservative backoff for 10m to let pool refill quickly. roll back after stable.
maya: initiating mitigation: bump warm_pool_target -> 30 via console now. @chris can you temporarily lower scale stabilization to 5s? need faster handoff.
chris: lowering stabilization to 5s for us-west for 15m window. applying.
infra-bot: infra-change: warm_pool_target updated from 18 -> 30 by maya
infra-bot: infra-change: stabilization_seconds updated from 30 -> 5 by chris
jin: started collecting perf profiles from new instances (perf counters + nvlink logs). uploading to /tmp/profiles/1805012345/
maya: after changes P90 dropped to ~160ms after ~3 minutes. still seeing occasional spikes to 300-400ms when a node gets scheduled away.
sre-oncall: created paged incident ticket INC-2026-0318-14. adding perf artifacts.
chris: root-cause hypothesis: combined effect of (1) kernel-selection tweak that increases cold-start kernel init time, (2) warm pool underprovisioned for burst distribution, (3) noisy neighbor NVLINK resets on certain hosts causing KV warm strategy to fall back to full fetch.
jin: evidence: perf profiles show a ~120ms added cost in kernel init path on cold node (malloc + kernel lookup). nvlink-reset logs align with high KV misses and increased PCIe retry counters.
maya: action items:
- chris: revert kernel-selection heuristic A/B and run canary with old behaviour for 2h (priority)
- jin: correlate NVLINK host IDs with provider host list + quarantine bad hosts (remove from warm pool)
- infra: consider marking the affected AZ sub-population as 'avoid' for warm pool placement until vendor confirms hardware flakiness
- ops: add a fastpath in provisioner to pre-populate KV cache from snapshot after boot to reduce kv_lookup_ms on new nodes
chris: started revert of kernel-selection tweak on canary (rolling 20% -> 100% over 2h if stable).
jin: flagged 3 host ids for quarantine: host-az3-114, host-az3-116, host-az3-119. sending to provider.
infra-bot: host-quarantine: host-az3-114,host-az3-116,host-az3-119 marked avoid-warmpool by jin
maya: nice work team. follow-up: schedule a post-incident retro tomorrow 10:00 PT, include perf team and infra vendor rep. capture changes to batching heuristics and kernel init path.
devex: logging reminder — add KV cache warm metrics to per-host exporter so we can alert on rising kv_lookup_ms and warm_pool hit-rate.
sre-oncall: incident status -> mitigated. monitoring for 30m. moving to postmortem once stable.
chris: note: need a longer-term fix in runtime: lazy-kernel-init should be async or deferred so provisioning doesn't block request path.
jin: also testing preheat of KV cache via snapshot injection; preliminary results show cold request kv_lookup_ms down from 430 -> 30.
maya: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem doc is linked.
